title: Macaroni with Creamy Cheese and Tuna

content.title: About
content.content: This dish consists of boiled macaroni coated with a creamy sauce that includes grated cheese and pieces of canned tuna. The combination of carbohydrates, protein, and fat makes it a filling and popular choice both at home and in cafeterias.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally, creamy pasta is made with short shapes like shells or penne so the sauce clings better.
Canned tuna is often used in quick‑prep meals because of its long shelf life and high protein content.
Cheese‑based creamy sauces appeared in European cuisine in the 19th century and have since become a staple for many pasta recipes.
The pairing of fish and dairy products is traditional in some Mediterranean regions.
The dish scales easily: a single serving can be multiplied by simply increasing the amount of pasta and sauce.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Tuna provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of omega‑3
items.content: Tuna contains polyunsaturated omega‑3 fatty acids that support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Hard cheese adds calcium, important for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Energy‑dense carbs
items.content: Macaroni supplies quick‑release carbohydrates, useful for active lifestyles.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cream and cheese provide vitamins B2 and B12, which play roles in metabolism.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: The creamy sauce and cheese make the dish calorie‑rich; portion control is advised for weight‑watching individuals.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Canned tuna is often salted, which can increase overall sodium intake.

items.title: Dairy allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: People with dairy sensitivities should use alternative sauces.

items.title: Food safety risk
items.content: Opened canned tuna must be stored properly; discard if it develops an off‑odor.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the macaroni hot, mixed with the creamy cheese‑tuna sauce. Optionally garnish with fresh herbs, black pepper, or a squeeze of lemon for extra brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2–3 days. When reheating, add a splash of milk or cream to restore the sauce’s creaminess.
